• **Clinical relevance:** Moderate.
• **Mechanism:** Ibuprofen (a non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drug, NSAID) can reduce prostaglandin‑mediated vasodilation in the afferent arteriole of the kidney. When combined with an ACE inhibitor such as ramipril, this may lead to a transient rise in serum creatinine, reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR), and, in susceptible patients, acute kidney injury (AKI).
• **Practical advice:** Use the lowest effective NSAID dose for the shortest duration possible. • **Regulatory note (Algeria):** The maximum approved dose for ibuprofen in Algeria is 2400 mg/day, but local guidelines may advise a lower limit for older adults. | | 3 | **What contraindications apply to this patient?** | • **Absolute contraindications for ibuprofen:**
 – Known hypersensitivity to NSAIDs or aspirin
